cases.label: exclusive
cases.note: Strictly after the start instant. croniter get_next, cron-parser, croner default.

cases.label: inclusive
cases.note: At or after. APScheduler's get_next_fire_time(None, now) and several schedulers' catch-up paths.

expectation.note: An off-by-one that duplicates or drops exactly one run, always at a boundary, and only when the caller's clock lands exactly on the schedule.

normative_evidence.note: crontab(5) describes a daemon matching the current minute; it says nothing about a 'next occurrence after T' API, which is a library invention

rationale: No cron document defines a 'next after T' function, so its inclusivity is a library policy. It is the most common source of duplicate-fire bugs in catch-up logic, and the corpus makes the axis explicit rather than picking a winner.
title: Start instant exactly on an occurrence: inclusive or exclusive?
